in_scene_decisions.summary: The backfill account quoted in nature above: rebuilt 2026-10-24 (JOB BOARD-SCENES-BACKFILL) from the piece’s production data; faithful, not modernized; the MP4 is not re-rendered from this scene. Alternatives recorded: leaving the YouTube embed (rejected: unwatchable for the owner); re-cutting to current law (rejected here: any re-edit is governed by the piece’s own lane).

‘The locked Lesson 1 poster script (files/short-01-agent-harness-poster-script.md): the poster IS the argument — one pile of material (model, instructions, memory, files, tools) built two ways: a mind standing apart vs the same material worn as a cortex. Spine in the build’s PLAN.md.’ Its context line carries the pair standing: ‘Lesson 1 pair verdict is Hadi’s (Action #34); both versions published 2026-10-21/22.’

‘The build’s own images in its own order: the poster compositions (scenes/sc_*.png) and the six-part panel lighting state by state (panel/state0–6.png) as the stack is named, each with the build’s measured zoompan move.’ Cuts sit on measured silence-detect run starts.

‘Reproduced exactly as published: the narration appears in timed chunks (the build’s captions.ass events — white DejaVu Sans bold with amber key chunks and cyan labels), each chunk fading in/out on its measured window. This is the proto word-animation form this generation of pieces was published with.’ Rebuilding the text as per-word DOM animation was rejected for the backfill (it would change the published piece); the treatment is flagged in the record, not silently changed.

‘The published MP4’s own audio track (short-01-agent-harness-poster.mp4), re-encoded to MP3 192k — the exact narration + music mix viewers heard, including container intro/outro audio where the wrap added it.’ (Here the word ‘published’ is exact: unlike the DIR trio’s drafts, this piece IS published — see render/verification.json.)

nature: A 2026-10-24 BACKFILL (JOB BOARD-SCENES-BACKFILL), stated in the scene’s own first decision record (DR-BACKFILL): the piece predates the HTML-SCENE LAW and the board could only offer a YouTube embed, which the owner’s phone walls with a bot check — Hadi at Action #34, 2026-10-24: ‘still the rendered video from youtube cannot watch. Need html format.’ The scene is rebuilt from the piece’s own production data — hidden_files/short01-poster/assemble.py’s segment table (22 segments with their zoompan moves), its captions.ass (53 timed text events) and its own scene/panel images — so the board plays the production file itself. In the scene’s own words: ‘Faithful, not modernized: same images, same words, same order, same timings as the published video.’ The original build’s renderer (the 2026-10-21 narration-first pipeline in hidden_files/short01-poster/) is NOT this file: this file is the backfill’s reconstruction of the published build, and the MP4 was NOT re-rendered from it. The package says so wherever the scene is described.

plan.agreement: The plan’s 127 word objects, read in order, reconstruct the locked script word-for-word on all 8 lines (verified at this migration, JOB MIGRATION-21; case-insensitive — 30 key words are uppercased in the plan for the amber display styling). The plan total (47.415147 s) is the scene’s own total and equals its embedded audio’s duration exactly; the render container measures 47.400 s and the narration track 47.396 s — three close figures, each attached to its own artefact; no identity is claimed beyond the measurements.
